meta.titre: Social Security and Social Insurance: protecting workers and their families against hardship
meta.sous_theme: Meaning, benefits and importance of social security in Cameroon

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A carpenter in Douala breaks his arm at work and cannot earn a wage for several months, yet rent, food and school fees still have to be paid. A teacher who has served for many years becomes too old to work. A young mother must stay at home to care for a newborn baby. Social security exists so that people in such situations, and their families, are not left without help. At the GCE you are asked to define it, to name the benefits it gives and to explain why it matters to workers.

items: A worker is a person who does a job in return for a wage or a salary.
An employer is a person or an organisation that pays workers for their labour.
Illness, accident, old age and the death of a breadwinner can all stop a person from earning money.
A contribution is a sum of money that is paid regularly into a common fund.

sections.titre: Social security and social insurance: meaning, benefits and importance
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Meaning
**Social security** is the set of measures by which a country protects people against the loss of income and the hardship caused by risks such as illness, accident at work, maternity, disability, old age and the death of the person who supports a family. Its **main aim** is to guarantee a decent standard of living to workers and their families when they cannot earn.

**Social insurance** is the main method. Workers and employers pay regular **contributions** into a common fund. When a worker suffers one of the risks, the fund pays a **benefit**.

### Social insurance and social assistance
| | Social insurance | Social assistance |
|---|---|---|
| Who pays | Workers and employers, through contributions | Mainly public funds |
| Who benefits | The insured worker and his or her family | Poor and vulnerable people who have no income, such as orphans, the elderly and persons with disabilities |
| Example in Cameroon | The National Social Insurance Fund (CNPS in French) | The government's social services |

### Benefits of the National Social Insurance Fund
- **Family benefits:** prenatal, maternity and family allowances.
- **Old-age pension** when a worker retires.
- **Invalidity pension** for a worker who can no longer work because of disability.
- **Survivors' benefits** for the family when the insured worker dies.
- **Compensation for work accidents and occupational diseases.**

The law requires employers to register their workers with the Fund and to pay contributions.

### Why social security is important to workers
- It gives an income in old age, so retirement does not mean poverty.
- It compensates a worker who is injured or made ill by the job.
- It helps parents to raise their children.
- It gives peace of mind, so workers can be more productive.
- It reduces poverty in the whole community.

### Family protection
The Constitution presents the family as the natural foundation of human society. Marriage is the legal basis of the family. Family allowances, family planning and health education all help parents to protect and raise their children.

variantes.nom: Questions on the aim of social security
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for the purpose or main aim
variantes.contenu_markdown: Answer with the idea of protection: to protect workers and their families against loss of income and hardship caused by social risks. Do not answer that it is to make workers rich or to give jobs, because creating jobs is a different government task.

variantes.nom: Questions on the importance to workers
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says describe or explain the importance
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write each point in three parts: the benefit, how it helps, and the result. Example: a pension is paid after retirement, so the old worker can buy food and medicine, and he is not a burden to his children. For a 7-mark question, give about four well developed points rather than seven bare words.

variantes.nom: Social insurance compared with social assistance
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks you to distinguish or compare the two
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use the table: insurance depends on contributions of the worker and the employer; assistance goes to people in need and does not depend on contributions.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain four ways in which membership of a social insurance scheme benefits a factory worker and his family. (8 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command word and count the points.
etapes.justification: Explain means that each way needs a reason or a result, and four ways are required.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Four ways, each with an explanation.

etapes.justification: Different benefits earn separate marks, while two points on pensions would share one mark.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Old-age pension, compensation for accidents, family allowances, survivors' benefits.

etapes.action: Write each point as benefit, help and result.
etapes.justification: This pattern turns a list into an explanation.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A pension gives a regular income after retirement, so the former worker can pay for food and care.

etapes.action: Link the points to the family.
etapes.justification: The question asks about the worker and his family, so at least two points must show the family gain.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Family allowances help to feed and school the children. Survivors' benefits support the widow and children after his death.

etapes.justification: A conclusion shows that you see the general purpose.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Social insurance protects the family from falling into poverty.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: First, the old-age pension gives the worker a regular income when he retires, so he can pay for food and medicine without depending on relatives. Second, if he is injured at work, the Fund pays compensation, so his family can survive while he recovers. Third, family allowances help him to feed and send his children to school. Fourth, if he dies, survivors' benefits support his wife and children. In short, social insurance protects the worker and his family from falling into poverty.

items.erreur_markdown: "Social security is a monthly sum that the government pays to every citizen."
items.pourquoi_faux: Social insurance benefits go to insured workers and their families who have paid contributions and who meet a risk. Help for the poor is social assistance, which is aimed at people in need and not at every citizen.
items.correction_markdown: Write that social security protects workers and their families against defined risks, and that social assistance helps vulnerable people.

items.erreur_markdown: "Social security protects workers only when they are old."
items.pourquoi_faux: Old age is only one risk. The Fund also pays family allowances, maternity benefits, compensation for accidents and invalidity, and survivors' benefits.
items.correction_markdown: Give a range of benefits: old-age, family, accident, invalidity and survivors.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Social Insurance Fund pays the worker's salary every month."
items.pourquoi_faux: The salary is paid by the employer for work done. The Fund pays benefits when the worker faces a risk or retires.
items.correction_markdown: Say that salaries come from employers, and benefits come from the Fund.

items.erreur_markdown: "Social insurance is paid for by the government alone."
items.pourquoi_faux: It is financed mainly by the contributions of employers and workers. This is why it is called insurance.
items.correction_markdown: State that employers and workers contribute to a common fund.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Define social security. (b) Name two benefits that a social insurance fund can give to the family of an insured worker.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Social security is the set of measures by which a country protects people against loss of income and hardship caused by risks such as illness, accident, maternity, disability, old age or death. (b) Any two: family allowances, maternity allowance, survivors' benefits, compensation for a work accident. Award marks for the definition and one mark for each benefit.

items.enonce_markdown: Mr Tabi is a registered worker in a sawmill. An accident at work leaves him unable to use his right arm. (a) Name one kind of benefit that may be paid to him. (b) Explain how it helps his family. (c) State one duty of his employer towards the social insurance scheme.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Compensation for a work accident, or an invalidity pension if he can no longer work. (b) It gives the family an income while he cannot earn a wage, so they can still pay for food, rent and school fees, and they do not have to beg for help. (c) The employer must register the worker with the Fund and pay the contributions due. Award marks for each correct answer with a reason.

items.enonce_markdown: Many young people who sell goods by the roadside or ride motorcycle taxis have no social insurance. (a) Explain two problems that this causes for them and their families. (b) Suggest two ways in which the protection of such workers can be improved.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Any two: when they fall ill or are injured, they have no income and no compensation; they have no pension, so old age means hardship; their children may leave school when money runs out; they depend on relatives or friends. (b) Any two: allow self-employed workers to join a scheme voluntarily; encourage savings groups and mutual aid associations; organise education campaigns about the advantages of insurance; help small businesses to register so that their workers can be covered. Award a mark for each problem and each way, and a mark for each explanation.

items_markdown: Social security is the set of measures that protect people against loss of income and hardship caused by risks such as illness, accident, maternity, disability, old age and death.
Social insurance works by contributions from workers and employers into a common fund that pays benefits.
Benefits include family allowances, old-age and invalidity pensions, survivors' benefits and compensation for work accidents.
Social assistance is different: it helps poor and vulnerable people and does not depend on contributions.
Social security gives workers income, security and peace of mind, and it reduces poverty.
Marriage is the legal basis of the family, and family allowances help parents to protect and raise their children.
